about: One cheap call per hosted model whose output the site quotes. drift_check.py calls each on the hosted MCP server and fails when a value leaves its tolerance, when provenance disagrees with the capability registry, or when the hosted source revision is not modal_app.py's pin. Expected values are the site's quoted figures; where a page shows the command but no number, the expected value is a regression pin from the committed pin and says so in 'basis'. Edit an expected value only with the page edit (or the evidence) in the same PR.

canaries.quote: a sustained +100bp lowers GDP by about £128m on impact, £406m by quarter 4, £472m by quarter 8 and £500m by quarter 12
canaries.basis: site quote; reproduces at OBR pin 0e44ec8 (October 2026 EFO, obr results/site_figures.json, run at b56fe3b; 0fe04c9 gave -128/-406/-475/-503 before the forecast population followed the EFO, obr #74), every quarter converged (6fbbe06 on the March 2026 EFO gave -129/-405/-480/-522; e4d7faa gave -121/-431/-482/-416)

canaries.quote: obr_shock reports real GDP, where the q12 ratio is 0.33 (tiles: 0.21 after 1 year and 0.37 after 3 years in current prices, against the OBR's published 0.3; the run uses the current £6.55bn costing)
canaries.basis: site quote; the 1p basic-rate costing (£6.55bn/yr = £1,637.5m/q) held on household income for an explicit 12-quarter window, so the ratio does not depend on score_reform's default window. Ratio = −ΔGDP(£m) / 1,637.5 (the add-factor carries the revenue raised, so GDP falls). 0e44ec8 (October 2026 EFO, local run 19 Nov 2026) gives 0.328 (−536.4 at q12); 0fe04c9 gave 0.330 (−540.2); 6fbbe06 gave 0.330 on £1,615.75m, e4d7faa 0.342, 1ed742c 0.357 (this is real GDP per current-price pound; the like-for-like current-price ratio is 0.374, obr #63/#66)

canaries.basis: site quote; us-frb-model 162cfe6 results/site_numbers.json (October 2026 LONGBASE): xgdp trough −0.5554 (2027Q4), lur peak +0.2758 (2028Q1)

canaries.quote: pe-macro hank-shock --kind monetary --size -0.0025 (command quoted; no number on the page)
canaries.basis: regression pin, not a site figure: the page quotes the command only. Hosted us-hank-model 19a8e5e on 6 Nov 2026 gave Y +0.361% on impact, reproduced locally at 58353e5 on 18 Nov 2026 (the +0.0025 run in r5/cross-model.md gave −0.36%, so the model is linear in the sign as expected) and +0.175% at quarter 3

canaries.quote: Live-facing fan chart; median from papers/boe-svar/figures/current_forecast.json, the archived 2026-11-12 round (6,000 draws): GDP 2026Q3 1.567, CPI 2026Q3 2.971
canaries.basis: site figure. The page shows the archived 12 Nov 2026 round (6,000 draws, 455 accepted, boe_var e7ad032); the hosted call runs 2,000 draws, so 0.1pp covers sampling noise. Since the 17f5d82 re-pin the hosted model also has a seasonally adjusted world CPI series (boe-var-model #34), which the archived round predates: a local 2,000-draw call at 17f5d82 on 21 Nov 2026 gave GDP 1.632 and CPI 2.879, 0.065 and 0.092 from the expected values, inside the tolerance but close to it for CPI. If this canary fails before a post-#34 round is archived, that gap is the first thing to check. Both use the simple YoY basis. A new data edge moves the first quarter and fails the label lookup, which is the point: the page would then be stale
